peer_results.rationale: BAC's candidates relate to municipal bond trusts and general long-term debt interest rates. While BAC discloses liquidity commitments to municipal bond trusts (bac_2024_8_D248), these are structurally distinct from Citi's credit card securitization Master Trust and multi-seller conduits. BAC's other candidate (bac_2024_8_D291) concerns aggregate long-term debt rates and does not address conduit structures or related maturities.

GS's candidates relate to real estate portfolio duration/yield (gs_2024_8_D137) and unsecured long-term borrowing interest rates (gs_2024_8_D336). These topics do not match Citi's specific disclosure regarding Master Trust note issuance to multi-seller conduits and their maturity profiles.

comparisons.peer_topic: Firm holdings and investment obligations in conduit commercial paper
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Firm held $2.9 billion and $9.8 billion, respectively, of commercial paper issued by Firm-administered multi-seller conduits, which were eliminated in consolidation. The Firm is not obligated to purchase this commercial paper except for amounts required by credit risk retention rules, and its investments reflect funding needs rather than market illiquidity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan disclose holdings in commercial paper issued by multi-seller conduits that they administer. Citi states that its Master Trust issues term notes to 'multi-seller commercial paper conduits' and provides the weighted-average maturity of these third-party notes (3.6 years in 2024). Similarly, JPMorgan discloses that it holds commercial paper issued by 'Firm-administered multi-seller conduits,' specifying the dollar amounts held ($2.9 billion in 2024). While Citi focuses on the issuance mechanics and maturity profile of the trust notes, JPMorgan focuses on the inventory of commercial paper holdings, both highlighting the operational link to multi-seller conduits.

sentences.text: Some of the term notes may be issued to multi-seller commercial paper conduits.
The weighted-average maturity of the third-party term notes issued by the Master Trust was 3.6 years as of December 31, 2024 and 3.8 years as of December 31, 2023.
In the normal course of business, JPMorganChase makes markets in and invests in commercial paper issued by the Firm-administered multi-seller conduits.

The Firm held $2.9 billion and $9.8 billion of the commercial paper issued by the Firm-administered multi-seller conduits at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, which have been eliminated in consolidation.
